outputs.L3:
The invention is intended to improve the processing of fluid materials, including operations such as emulsification, dispersion, dissolution, atomization, mixing, and stirring. It is particularly suitable for applications in which a material to be processed must be subjected to strong and efficient mechanical action in order to obtain a uniform or finely processed state.

The device employs a rotor-stator type mixer installed inside a processing tank. In this configuration, a rotor is rotated at high speed relative to a stator, thereby applying shear force, impact, turbulence, and flow action to the processing object. As a result, the fluid material introduced into the tank can be efficiently mixed, dispersed, emulsified, dissolved, atomized, or otherwise processed.

During operation, the processing tank may be maintained under various pressure conditions depending on the nature of the material and the intended processing result. For example, the tank may be kept in a pressurized state, operated at atmospheric pressure, or maintained in a vacuum state. This flexibility allows the device to be used for a wide range of processing conditions and materials.

A significant feature of the invention is that the mechanism actively suppresses or prevents the occurrence of negative pressure on the inner diameter side of the rotor. In conventional rotor-stator mixers, rotation of the rotor may create a region of reduced pressure near the inner diameter side, which can lead to undesirable effects such as cavitation, gas entrainment, unstable flow, or deterioration in processing efficiency. By preventing or reducing such negative pressure, the invention enables more stable operation and improves the quality and consistency of the processed material.

When the rotor rotates, it causes the processing object to flow through the mixer while maintaining the material at or above a predetermined pressure. This controlled pressure flow ensures that the material is effectively acted upon by the rotor and stator without pressure dropping to an undesirable level. Consequently, the invention enhances the efficiency and reliability of fluid processing and makes it possible to perform emulsification, dispersion, dissolution, atomization, mixing, or stirring in a stable and controlled manner.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a fluid processing apparatus and method for improving operations such as emulsification, dispersion, dissolution, atomization, mixing, and stirring of a processing object. The processing object may be a liquid, a mixture of liquids, a liquid containing solids, a liquid containing gas, or another fluid material that requires uniform treatment. The apparatus includes a processing tank that can be maintained under a selected internal condition, such as pressurized conditions, atmospheric pressure, or reduced-pressure/vacuum conditions, depending on the requirements of the material and the intended process.

Inside the processing tank, a rotor-stator type mixer is provided. The mixer includes a rotor that rotates at high speed and a stator arranged in proximity to the rotor. When the rotor is driven, the processing object is drawn into the region between the rotor and the stator, subjected to strong shear force, turbulence, impact, and pressure fluctuation, and then discharged outward. Through this action, droplets, particles, aggregates, or other non-uniform portions of the processing object can be finely divided and uniformly distributed. As a result, emulsification, dispersion, dissolution, atomization, mixing, or stirring can be performed more efficiently and with improved uniformity.

In conventional rotor-stator mixers, the rotation of the rotor may generate a localized negative pressure near the central region of the rotor. Such negative pressure can cause undesirable phenomena, including cavitation, gas entrainment, foaming, unstable flow, uneven processing, reduced treatment efficiency, or damage to the material being processed. These problems are particularly significant when the processing tank is operated under vacuum or when the fluid has characteristics that make it sensitive to pressure changes.

To address these issues, the invention provides a mechanism for suppressing the formation of negative pressure near the center of the rotor. The mechanism is configured so that the processing object flowing toward or around the rotor center is maintained at or above a predetermined pressure. By preventing the pressure from falling below this predetermined level, the apparatus stabilizes the flow of the processing object and suppresses the occurrence of cavitation or other adverse effects associated with negative pressure.

The apparatus may be configured as an atomization device in which the rotating rotor causes the processing object to flow under controlled pressure conditions. The rotor applies rotational energy to the processing object, and the interaction between the rotor and the stator generates fine atomization, emulsification, dispersion, or mixing. At the same time, the pressure-suppressing mechanism ensures that the central region of the rotor does not become excessively depressurized. This enables the processing object to be treated effectively even under conditions where conventional devices would suffer from unstable suction, foaming, or insufficient processing performance.

Accordingly, the invention makes it possible to carry out high-efficiency fluid processing in a sealed processing tank while controlling the pressure environment. The processing tank may be operated under pressure, at atmospheric pressure, or under vacuum, and the rotor-stator mixer can perform stable treatment in each of these environments. By maintaining the processing object at or above the predetermined pressure during rotor operation, the invention improves the quality and reliability of emulsification, dispersion, dissolution, atomization, mixing, and stirring, while reducing or preventing undesirable negative-pressure conditions near the rotor center.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it is used when we are talking about something specific or already known to the listener or reader.

For example, when we say, “I saw a dog,” we mean any dog. But when we say, “I saw the dog,” we are talking about a particular dog. This small word helps make meaning clear and precise.

“The” appears everywhere: in books, conversations, songs, news, and instructions. It helps connect ideas and guide the reader toward a specific person, place, object, or idea. Although it is short and simple, “the” is essential for fluent and natural English.

In many ways, “the” shows that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an “object of the invention” and summary paragraph for a patent about a rotor-stator mixer mechanism that processes fluid materials in a tank and suppresses negative pressure on the inner diameter side of the rotor.
counterfactuals.output:
**Object of the Invention**

An object of the invention is to provide a rotor-stator mixer mechanism for processing fluid materials in a tank, which is capable of efficiently imparting shear, circulation, dispersion, emulsification, or mixing action to the fluid material while suppressing generation of negative pressure on an inner diameter side of a rotor. Another object of the invention is to reduce the tendency of air entrainment, cavitation, foaming, or unstable flow caused by localized suction at the rotor inner periphery, thereby improving processing stability and product quality. A further object of the invention is to provide a rotor-stator mixer structure in which fluid flow toward and through the rotor-stator region is controlled so that pressure balance is maintained around the rotor, while the desired high-shear processing effect between the rotor and stator is preserved.

**Summary of the Invention**

According to one aspect, the invention provides a rotor-stator mixer mechanism disposed in a tank containing a fluid material to be processed. The mechanism includes a rotor configured to rotate about an axis and a stator arranged adjacent to the rotor so as to define a processing region in which the fluid material is subjected to shear and mixing forces. The rotor is provided with flow-control features configured to suppress formation of negative pressure on an inner diameter side of the rotor during rotation. In certain embodiments, the flow-control features may include one or more passages, openings, guide surfaces, relief channels, vanes, or pressure-balancing regions that permit or promote controlled movement of fluid toward the inner diameter side of the rotor, thereby reducing localized suction while maintaining discharge of the fluid material through the rotor-stator processing region. By suppressing negative pressure at the rotor inner diameter, the mixer mechanism can reduce cavitation, foaming, gas entrainment, vibration, and nonuniform processing, and can improve the consistency and efficiency of fluid material treatment within the tank.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Japanese patent translation-style description for an atomization device comprising a rotor-stator type mixer in a processing tank, where the rotor causes the processing object to flow at a predetermined pressure or higher.
counterfactuals.output:
【発明の名称】  
微粒化装置

【技術分野】  
本発明は、処理対象物を微粒化、乳化、分散又は混合するための微粒化装置に関し、特に、処理槽内に配置されたロータ・ステータ型ミキサを用いて、処理対象物を所定圧力以上で流動させる微粒化装置に関する。

【背景技術】  
従来、液体、懸濁液、スラリー、乳化液等の処理対象物を微粒化する装置として、ロータとステータとの間の剪断力を利用するロータ・ステータ型ミキサが知られている。この種の装置では、ロータの回転により処理対象物をステータの開口部又は隙間に通過させ、剪断、衝突、乱流等によって粒子径又は液滴径を低減する。

【発明の概要】  
本発明の一態様に係る微粒化装置は、処理対象物を収容する処理槽と、前記処理槽内に設けられたロータ・ステータ型ミキサと、を備える。前記ロータ・ステータ型ミキサは、回転可能に配置されたロータと、前記ロータの周囲又は近傍に配置されたステータとを有する。前記ロータは、回転により前記処理対象物を吸引又は押送し、前記処理対象物を前記ロータと前記ステータとの間又は前記ステータに形成された開口部を通して流動させるように構成されている。さらに、前記ロータは、前記処理対象物が所定圧力以上となる流動圧力で流動するように構成されている。

この構成によれば、処理槽内の処理対象物を、ロータの回転によって所定圧力以上でロータ・ステータ部に導くことができるため、処理対象物に対して高い剪断力、衝突力及び乱流エネルギを付与することができる。これにより、処理対象物の微粒化効率を向上させることができる。

【発明を実施するための形態】  
以下、本発明の一実施形態に係る微粒化装置について説明する。

本実施形態の微粒化装置は、処理対象物を収容可能な処理槽と、前記処理槽内に配置されたロータ・ステータ型ミキサと、前記ロータを回転駆動する駆動部とを備える。処理対象物は、例えば、液体、固液混合物、液液混合物、スラリー、懸濁液、乳化液、樹脂材料、食品材料、医薬材料、化粧品材料又は化学材料であってよい。

ロータ・ステータ型ミキサは、回転軸に連結されたロータと、ロータの外周側に配置されたステータとを含む。ロータは、羽根部、溝部、突出部又は流路形成部を有してもよい。ステータは、複数の孔、スリット、切欠き又は流通開口を有してもよい。ロータが回転すると、処理槽内の処理対象物はロータ側に吸引され、ロータとステータとの間の隙間、又はステータの開口部を通過する。この際、処理対象物には、剪断作用、圧縮作用、衝突作用及びキャビテーション作用の少なくとも一つが付与される。

本実施形態において、ロータは、処理対象物を所定圧力以上で流動させるように構成されている。ここで、所定圧力は、処理対象物の種類、粘度、目的粒径、処理量等に応じて適宜設定される。例えば、所定圧力は、処理対象物がステータの開口部又はロータとステータとの隙間を通過する際に発生する流動圧力であってよい。また、所定圧力は、処理槽内の静圧、ロータ近傍の局所圧力、又はステータ通過時の差圧として規定されてもよい。

ロータが処理対象物を所定圧力以上で流動させるために、ロータの回転数、羽根形状、羽根角度、ロータ径、ロータとステータとの隙間寸法、ステータ開口面積、処理槽内の液位、又は処理対象物の循環経路が設定されてもよい。例えば、ロータの回転により、処理対象物がロータ中心部から外周部へ圧送され、ステータの開口部を通過する際に所定圧力以上の流動状態が形成される。

処理槽は、密閉型又は開放型のいずれであってもよい。密閉型の場合、処理槽内を加圧状態に保持することにより、ロータによって生じる流動圧力と相まって、処理対象物にさらに高い処理エネルギを付与することができる。また、処理槽には、処理対象物を供給する供給口、処理後の処理対象物を排出する排出口、圧力を検出する圧力センサ、温度を検出する温度センサ、又は処理対象物を冷却若しくは加熱する温調部が設けられてもよい。

微粒化装置は、圧力センサの検出値に基づいてロータの回転数を制御する制御部をさらに備えてもよい。制御部は、処理対象物の流動圧力が前記所定圧力未満である場合にロータの回転数を上昇させ、前記流動圧力が所定圧力以上に維持されるように制御してもよい。これにより、処理対象物の粘度変化や処理量変動が生じた場合であっても、安定した微粒化処理を行うことができる。

【作用効果】  
本発明によれば、処理槽内にロータ・ステータ型ミキサを備え、ロータが処理対象物を所定圧力以上で流動させるため、処理対象物に対して十分な剪断力及び乱流エネルギを付与することができる。その結果、粒子又は液滴の微細化を効率的に行うことができ、均一性の高い処理物を得ることができる。

また、処理対象物が処理槽内で循環しながらロータ・ステータ部を通過するため、処理対象物全体に対して均質な微粒化処理を施すことができる。さらに、流動圧力を所定圧力以上に維持することにより、処理条件の再現性を向上させることができる。

【特許請求の範囲】  
【請求項１】  
処理対象物を収容する処理槽と、  
前記処理槽内に配置されたロータ・ステータ型ミキサと、を備え、  
前記ロータ・ステータ型ミキサは、回転可能なロータと、前記ロータの近傍に配置されたステータとを有し、  
前記ロータは、回転により前記処理対象物を前記ステータに向けて流動させ、かつ、前記処理対象物を所定圧力以上で流動させるように構成されている、  
微粒化装置。

【請求項２】  
前記ステータは、前記処理対象物が通過する複数の開口部を有し、  
前記処理対象物は、前記ロータの回転によって前記開口部を通過する、  
請求項１に記載の微粒化装置。

【請求項３】  
前記処理対象物の圧力を検出する圧力センサと、  
前記圧力センサの検出値に基づいて前記ロータの回転数を制御する制御部と、をさらに備える、  
請求項１又は２に記載の微粒化装置。

【請求項４】  
前記制御部は、前記処理対象物の圧力が前記所定圧力未満である場合に前記ロータの回転数を増加させる、  
請求項３に記載の微粒化装置。

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a concise patent specification excerpt describing an atomization device for fluid processing, including emulsification, dispersion, dissolution, atomization, mixing, and stirring, operable under pressurized, atmospheric, or vacuum tank conditions.
counterfactuals.output:
An atomization device for fluid processing comprises a rotatable shaft extending into a processing tank and carrying an atomizing head configured to receive one or more fluids and discharge the fluids as fine droplets, films, or streams under shear generated by rotation of the head. The device is adapted for use in emulsification, dispersion, dissolution, atomization, mixing, and stirring operations, either individually or in combination.

The atomizing head may include a fluid inlet, a distribution chamber, and one or more discharge openings, grooves, vanes, teeth, or peripheral edges for accelerating and atomizing the supplied fluid into a surrounding liquid or gas phase within the tank. Rotation of the shaft produces centrifugal force and shear at the discharge region, thereby promoting particle size reduction, interfacial contact, and uniform distribution of components. The device may further include a stator, baffle, guide member, or recirculation structure positioned adjacent to the atomizing head to enhance mixing efficiency and control flow patterns.

The shaft is supported by a drive unit located outside the tank and may pass through a sealing assembly selected for operation under positive pressure, atmospheric pressure, or vacuum conditions. The sealing assembly may comprise a mechanical seal, magnetic coupling, gland seal, or other pressure-retaining structure, enabling the tank to be operated as a closed vessel during processing. The atomization device may be mounted from the top, side, or bottom of the tank and may be configured for batch or continuous fluid processing.

In operation, fluid supplied to the atomizing head and/or present in the tank is subjected to centrifugal atomization, turbulent shear, and circulation generated by rotation of the head. The device thereby facilitates rapid emulsification of immiscible liquids, dispersion of solids or additives, dissolution of soluble materials, atomization of liquids into a gaseous or liquid medium, and general mixing or stirring within tanks maintained under pressurized, atmospheric, or vacuum conditions.
